```{python}
# | label: setup
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib as mpl
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from IPython.display import Markdown

# Locate the repository root, so this report may live at any depth under it.
_root = next(p for p in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents]
             if (p / "pixi.toml").exists())
sys.path.insert(0, str(_root / "src"))
from arkhinfra import v3_common as c  # noqa: E402
from arkhinfra import egais as e  # noqa: E402

mpl.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "DejaVu Sans",   # full Cyrillic coverage for figure labels
    "figure.dpi": 150,
    "axes.spines.top": False,
    "axes.spines.right": False,
    "axes.grid": True,
    "grid.alpha": 0.25,
    "axes.titlesize": 12,
    "axes.titleweight": "bold",
})

ACCENT, RISK, GREEN, PURPLE = c.ACCENT, c.RISK, c.GREEN, c.PURPLE
MIXED, OLD = c.MIXED, c.OLD
INK = "#1f2933"

# Licence state keeps a fixed assignment: one colour for "in force", one for
# every way of being out of force, so the two never swap between charts.
STATUS_COLORS = {
    "Active": GREEN, "Expired": OLD, "Terminated": MIXED,
    "Reissued": PURPLE, "Annulled": RISK,
}


def barh(series, title, xlabel, color=ACCENT, fmt_pct=False, figsize=(7.2, 4.4)):
    s = series.sort_values(ascending=True)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
    ax.barh(s.index, s.values, color=color)
    total = s.sum()
    for y, v in enumerate(s.values):
        lbl = f"{v:,} ({v / total * 100:.0f}%)" if fmt_pct else f"{v:,}"
        ax.text(v, y, " " + lbl, va="center", ha="left", fontsize=8, color=INK)
    ax.set_xlabel(xlabel)
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.margins(x=0.16)
    ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```

```{python}
# | label: load
eg = e.load_egais()
v3 = c.load_v3()
v3["category_2022"] = c.recode_2022(v3)

eg["okrug_key"], eg["okrug_source"] = e.assign_okrug(eg, v3)

n_rows = len(eg)
n_lic = eg["licence_no"].nunique()
n_addr = eg["outlet_address"].nunique()
n_org = eg["org_inn"].nunique()

active = eg[eg["is_active"]]
retail = eg[eg["is_active"] & eg["is_retail"]]
n_active, n_retail = len(active), len(retail)

OKRUG_ORDER = [k for k in eg["okrug_key"].value_counts().index if k != "Unknown"]
```

# Introduction

This report profiles a source that was **not commissioned**: the state
consolidated register of licences, published as open data by
Росалкогольтабакконтроль and downloaded as a 10.9 GB XML covering the whole
country. Unlike every delivery so far, nothing about it was specified by
this project — it is a public register that happens to record, for every
licensed outlet in Arkhangelsk, an address and often a coordinate pair.

Two facts about it govern everything that follows, and neither is visible from
the dataset's title.

## It holds alcohol licences, not tobacco

The regulator's remit covers both alcohol and tobacco, and the register was
approached in the expectation of tobacco retail. It contains none. Every one of
the `{python} f"{n_rows:,}"` Arkhangelsk records is an alcohol or ethanol
licence, so for this project the register is a **risk-factor layer**, parallel
to the `Alcohol shops` class of the commissioned exports — not a new
health-supporting one, and not a tobacco source.

## It is a register, not a list of open outlets

Only `{python} f"{n_active:,}"` of the `{python} f"{n_rows:,}"` rows
(`{python} f"{n_active / n_rows * 100:.0f}"` %) are licences still in force.
The rest expired, were terminated, reissued or annulled, and they keep their
historic address — a register accumulates, it does not refresh. Every count in
this report that is meant to describe the city today is taken from the active
subset.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-shape
# | tbl-cap: "What the extract contains. A row is an outlet-licence pair: one licence covers many outlets."
rows = [
    ["Rows in the extract", f"{n_rows:,}"],
    ["Distinct licences", f"{n_lic:,}"],
    ["Distinct outlet addresses", f"{n_addr:,}"],
    ["Distinct organisations (INN)", f"{n_org:,}"],
    ["Licences in force", f"{n_active:,}"],
    ["In force and retail-facing", f"{n_retail:,}"],
    ["With usable coordinates", f"{int(eg['has_coords'].sum()):,}"],
]
Markdown(pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["", "Value"]).to_markdown(index=False))
```

# Part I — extraction {#sec-extract}

The register ships as one 10.9 GB XML holding **1,660,448 records** for the
whole country, which does not fit in memory. `scripts/parse_egais.py`
(`pixi run parse-egais`) reads it in 16 MiB chunks, cuts them on the `</row>`
boundary, and hands to the XML parser only those segments whose raw bytes
already contain "Архангельск". That is a substring test over the whole file and
a real parse over the 12,311 records that survive it; the pass takes about six
minutes and never holds more than one chunk plus the matched rows.

Of those 12,311 mentions, `{python} f"{n_rows:,}"` have an **outlet** address in
the city itself. The remainder name the region, a different settlement in it, or
an Arkhangelsk-registered company trading elsewhere.

## The published schema does not describe the published file

The dataset ships an XSD. It is wrong. The schema declares `Details/Detail`
elements carrying the data as **attributes**; the file delivers `data/row` with
the data in **child elements**, and several names differ between the two —
including the register's own typo, `Дата__время_и_место_выезного_обслуживания`.
A parser written from the documentation returns nothing at all. The field map in
`parse_egais.py` follows the file.

## What was carried across

Of the register's 24 fields, `{python} "20"` are kept and four dropped. The
dropped ones are the per-licence change history (a long free-text field that
would have dominated the output size), the blank-form number, and the two
mobile-service fields — all either empty throughout or irrelevant to spatial
work. The result is a 2.0 MB TSV.

```{python}
# | label: fig-completeness
# | fig-cap: "Field completeness in the extract. Two fields are empty for every record; coordinates reach just over half."
cols = ["licence_no", "status", "date_issued", "org_name", "org_inn",
        "outlet_address", "outlet_street", "outlet_house", "org_email",
        "licence_prev_no", "coords_raw", "products"]
fill = pd.Series({col: (eg[col].astype(str).str.strip() != "").mean() * 100
                  for col in cols}).sort_values()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.2))
colors = [RISK if v < 60 else ACCENT for v in fill.values]
ax.barh(fill.index, fill.values, color=colors)
for y, v in enumerate(fill.values):
    ax.text(v, y, f" {v:.0f}%", va="center", ha="left", fontsize=8, color=INK)
ax.set_xlim(0, 108)
ax.set_xlabel("Records with a value, %")
ax.set_title("Field completeness — licence register extract")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

`Виды_продукции` (product types) is empty for every single record, as is the
blank-form number — the same pattern of declared-but-unpopulated fields the
third delivery showed with `website_check_status`.

# Part II — the licence portfolio {#sec-portfolio}

```{python}
# | label: fig-activity
# | fig-cap: "Licensed activity. Two retail classes account for almost everything; wholesale, transport and production are marginal."
barh(eg["activity_class"].value_counts(),
     "Licensed activity — all records", "Licences", color=ACCENT, fmt_pct=True,
     figsize=(7.2, 3.4))
```

The register distinguishes **off-trade** retail (a shop selling sealed bottles)
from **on-trade** retail, where the same licence also covers consumption on the
premises — a bar, a café, a restaurant. That distinction matters for a health
study: the two have different exposure profiles, and the commissioned exports
carry no equivalent of it anywhere.

```{python}
# | label: fig-status
# | fig-cap: "Licence state. Expired and terminated records outnumber those in force by nearly three to one."
counts = eg["status_en"].value_counts().reindex(e.STATUS_ORDER).dropna()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.2))
ax.barh(counts.index[::-1], counts.values[::-1],
        color=[STATUS_COLORS[k] for k in counts.index[::-1]])
for y, v in enumerate(counts.values[::-1]):
    ax.text(v, y, f" {v:,} ({v / n_rows * 100:.0f}%)", va="center", ha="left",
            fontsize=8, color=INK)
ax.set_xlabel("Records")
ax.set_title("Licence state — all records")
ax.margins(x=0.18)
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The register writes the same expiry state two ways — `истекла` and
`срок действия истек` — which are folded together here. A consumer that treats
them as distinct states undercounts expiry.

```{python}
# | label: fig-timeline
# | fig-cap: "Licences by year of issue. The 2012 spike is a licensing-regime artefact, not a wave of openings."
by_year = eg["issue_year"].value_counts().sort_index()
by_year = by_year[by_year.index >= 2006]
act_year = eg[eg["is_active"]]["issue_year"].value_counts().reindex(by_year.index).fillna(0)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.6))
ax.bar(by_year.index, by_year.values, color=OLD, label="All licences")
ax.bar(act_year.index, act_year.values, color=GREEN, label="Still in force")
ax.set_xlabel("Year of issue")
ax.set_ylabel("Licences")
ax.set_title("Licences issued per year")
ax.legend(fontsize=8)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Issue dates run 2006–2026 and peak sharply in **2012**, when
`{python} f"{int(by_year.get(2012, 0)):,}"` licences were issued — more than any
three other years together. That is a re-registration wave under a changed
licensing regime, not a burst of new shops, and it is a trap for anyone reading
the register as a business-formation time series.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-orgs
# | tbl-cap: "The ten organisations holding the most outlets currently in force. Federal chains dominate."
short = active["org_name"].str.extract(r"Сокращенно:\s*(.+)$")[0].fillna(active["org_name"])
top = short.str.replace(r'^["\s]+|["\s]+$', "", regex=True).value_counts().head(10)
tbl = pd.DataFrame({"Organisation": [s[:44] for s in top.index],
                    "Outlets in force": top.values})
tbl["Share"] = [f"{v / n_active * 100:.1f}%" for v in top.values]
Markdown(tbl.to_markdown(index=False))
```

Ownership is concentrated: the top ten holders account for
`{python} f"{top.sum() / n_active * 100:.0f}"` % of all outlets currently in
force, and the single largest — the Bristol chain — for
`{python} f"{top.iloc[0] / n_active * 100:.0f}"` %. Alcohol availability in the
city is therefore set by a handful of federal retail decisions rather than by
many independent operators, which is a policy-relevant finding in itself.

# Part III — recovering geography {#sec-geo}

The register records **no okrug**. Since okrug is the unit every other report in
this project works in, it has to be recovered, and `arkhinfra.egais.assign_okrug`
does it by two routes in order of trust:

1. **Coordinates** — the nearest object in the third-delivery export within
   400 m lends its okrug.
2. **Street name** — for rows without a usable coordinate, the okrug most of
   that street's export objects sit in.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-okrug-source
# | tbl-cap: "How each row's okrug was recovered. The weaker street route carries a third of the extract; nothing rests on it alone in the active subset."
src_all = eg["okrug_source"].value_counts()
src_act = active["okrug_source"].value_counts()
tbl = pd.DataFrame({
    "Route": ["Coordinates (≤400 m)", "Street name", "Unassigned"],
    "All rows": [src_all.get("coordinates", 0), src_all.get("street", 0),
                 src_all.get("unassigned", 0)],
    "In force": [src_act.get("coordinates", 0), src_act.get("street", 0),
                 src_act.get("unassigned", 0)],
})
tbl["All %"] = [f"{v / n_rows * 100:.0f}%" for v in tbl["All rows"]]
tbl["In force %"] = [f"{v / n_active * 100:.0f}%" for v in tbl["In force"]]
for col in ("All rows", "In force"):
    tbl[col] = tbl[col].map(lambda v: f"{v:,}")
Markdown(tbl.to_markdown(index=False))
```

Coordinates cover `{python} f"{eg['has_coords'].mean() * 100:.0f}"` % of rows.
They are published as degrees-minutes-seconds strings, and eight of them are
plainly wrong — a dropped leading digit places an Arkhangelsk café at longitude
10.55°, in the North Sea. Those are flagged rather than silently mapped.

```{python}
# | label: fig-okrug
# | fig-cap: "Licences in force per okrug, against the third-delivery export's Alcohol shops class in the same okrug."
ok_act = retail["okrug_key"].value_counts().reindex(OKRUG_ORDER).fillna(0)
v3_alc = (v3[v3["category_2022"] == "Alcohol shops"]["okrug_key"]
          .value_counts().reindex(OKRUG_ORDER).fillna(0))
y = np.arange(len(OKRUG_ORDER))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.6))
ax.barh(y + 0.2, ok_act.values, height=0.4, color=RISK, label=f"Licences in force ({int(ok_act.sum()):,})")
ax.barh(y - 0.2, v3_alc.values, height=0.4, color=OLD, label=f"Export 'Alcohol shops' ({int(v3_alc.sum()):,})")
for i, v in enumerate(ok_act.values):
    ax.text(v, i + 0.2, f" {int(v)}", va="center", fontsize=7.5, color=INK)
for i, v in enumerate(v3_alc.values):
    ax.text(v, i - 0.2, f" {int(v)}", va="center", fontsize=7.5, color=INK)
ax.set_yticks(y, OKRUG_ORDER)
ax.set_xlabel("Objects")
ax.set_title("Licensed alcohol retail vs. the commissioned export")
ax.margins(x=0.16)
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="lower right")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The register puts the most licensed outlets in **Lomonosovsky** and
**Oktyabrsky**, the two central okrugs — the same pair the export ranks highest,
so the two sources agree on shape. They disagree sharply on magnitude, which is
@sec-crosscheck.

# Part IV — spatial distribution {#sec-map}

```{python}
# | label: fig-map
# | fig-cap: "Licensed alcohol outlets currently in force, on an OpenStreetMap/CARTO basemap. Only rows with a usable published coordinate are shown."
pts = retail[retail["has_coords"]]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 6.4))
ax.scatter(pts["longitude"], pts["latitude"], s=16, alpha=0.8,
           color=RISK, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.3,
           label=f"Licence in force ({len(pts):,})")
ax.set_xlabel("Longitude")
ax.set_ylabel("Latitude")
ax.set_title("Licensed alcohol retail — outlets in force")
ax.set_aspect(1 / np.cos(np.deg2rad(64.54)))
try:
    # Tiles are cached in data/tile_cache, so only the first render needs
    # internet access; offline we fall back to the plain scatter.
    import contextily as ctx
    tile_cache = c.ROOT / "data" / "tile_cache"
    tile_cache.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    ctx.set_cache_dir(str(tile_cache))
    ctx.add_basemap(ax, crs="EPSG:4326", source=ctx.providers.CartoDB.Positron,
                    attribution_size=5)
    ax.grid(visible=False)
except Exception:
    ax.grid(alpha=0.2)
ax.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=8, markerscale=1.6, framealpha=0.9)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
# | label: fig-map-trade
# | fig-cap: "Off-trade outlets (shops, orange) against on-trade (bars and cafés, blue). On-trade clusters in the historic centre; off-trade follows residential districts outward."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 6.4))
for key, color in [(e.ACTIVITY_EN["retail"], RISK),
                   (e.ACTIVITY_EN["catering"], ACCENT)]:
    sub = pts[pts["activity_class"] == key]
    ax.scatter(sub["longitude"], sub["latitude"], s=18, alpha=0.8,
               color=color, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.3,
               label=f"{key} ({len(sub):,})")
ax.set_xlabel("Longitude")
ax.set_ylabel("Latitude")
ax.set_title("Off-trade and on-trade alcohol retail")
ax.set_aspect(1 / np.cos(np.deg2rad(64.54)))
try:
    import contextily as ctx
    tile_cache = c.ROOT / "data" / "tile_cache"
    tile_cache.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    ctx.set_cache_dir(str(tile_cache))
    ctx.add_basemap(ax, crs="EPSG:4326", source=ctx.providers.CartoDB.Positron,
                    attribution_size=5)
    ax.grid(visible=False)
except Exception:
    ax.grid(alpha=0.2)
ax.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=8, markerscale=1.6, framealpha=0.9)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Distance from the city centre, to check the visual claim rather than assert it.
_d = c.haversine_m(pts["latitude"], pts["longitude"], 64.5393, 40.5180)
_by = pd.DataFrame({"cls": pts["activity_class"].to_numpy(), "d": _d}).groupby("cls")["d"].median()
med_on = _by.get(e.ACTIVITY_EN["catering"], np.nan)
med_off = _by.get(e.ACTIVITY_EN["retail"], np.nan)
```

The split is spatially real, not decorative: measured from the city centre, the
median on-trade outlet sits `{python} f"{med_on / 1000:.1f}"` km out and the
median off-trade outlet `{python} f"{med_off / 1000:.1f}"` km — bars and cafés
hold the historic centre while shops follow housing outward.

Note what the map cannot show. Coordinates are absent for
`{python} f"{(1 - eg['has_coords'].mean()) * 100:.0f}"` % of the extract, and
their presence is not random — they became a licensing requirement partway
through the period, so older licences lack them. A map of this register is
therefore biased toward **recently issued** outlets, and its density should not
be read as a complete surface.

# Part V — against the commissioned export {#sec-crosscheck}

The third delivery classifies `{python} f"{int((v3['category_2022'] == 'Alcohol shops').sum()):,}"`
of its 7,263 objects as `Alcohol shops`, city-wide. The register lists
`{python} f"{n_retail:,}"` alcohol retail licences **currently in force**, one
per address. The export therefore accounts for roughly a **fifth** of the city's
licensed alcohol retail.

```{python}
# | label: match
pts_m = retail[retail["has_coords"]]
ref = v3.dropna(subset=["latitude", "longitude"])
d = c.haversine_m(pts_m["latitude"].to_numpy()[:, None],
                  pts_m["longitude"].to_numpy()[:, None],
                  ref["latitude"].to_numpy()[None, :],
                  ref["longitude"].to_numpy()[None, :])
near = d.argmin(axis=1)
dist = d[np.arange(len(pts_m)), near]
within = dist <= 50
near_cat = pd.Series(ref["category_2022"].to_numpy()[near[within]])
cov = within.mean() * 100
```

This is not, however, a coverage failure. Taking every licensed outlet with a
usable coordinate and asking what the export holds nearest to it,
`{python} f"{cov:.0f}"` % have some export object within 50 m — the export knows
about the buildings. What it does not know is that alcohol is sold in them.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-nearest
# | tbl-cap: "What the export calls the object nearest each licensed outlet (within 50 m). Licensed alcohol retail is overwhelmingly filed as something else."
vc = near_cat.value_counts()
tbl = pd.DataFrame({"Export class of nearest object": vc.index,
                    "Outlets": vc.values,
                    "Share": [f"{v / vc.sum() * 100:.0f}%" for v in vc.values]})
Markdown(tbl.to_markdown(index=False))
```

The reason is structural, not a defect in the contractor's work. A Russian
grocery chain sells alcohol under a licence held by the shop; the shop is a
`Продуктовый магазин` in any directory, and only a **specialised** alcohol shop
is ever labelled as one. The export's `Alcohol shops` class counts shopfronts
named for alcohol; the register counts the legal right to sell it. The second is
what a health study means by exposure.

```{python}
# | label: fig-crosscheck
# | fig-cap: "Alcohol availability per okrug under the two definitions. The register lifts every okrug, and reorders the middle of the ranking."
comp = pd.DataFrame({
    "Register (in force)": retail["okrug_key"].value_counts(),
    "Export (Alcohol shops)": v3[v3["category_2022"] == "Alcohol shops"]["okrug_key"].value_counts(),
}).reindex(OKRUG_ORDER).fillna(0)
comp["ratio"] = comp["Register (in force)"] / comp["Export (Alcohol shops)"].replace(0, np.nan)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.8))
ax.bar(range(len(comp)), comp["ratio"].values, color=PURPLE)
for i, v in enumerate(comp["ratio"].values):
    if np.isfinite(v):
        ax.text(i, v, f"{v:.1f}×", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=8, color=INK)
ax.set_xticks(range(len(comp)), comp.index, rotation=35, ha="right", fontsize=8)
ax.set_ylabel("Register ÷ export")
ax.set_title("How much alcohol retail the export misses, by okrug")
ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The undercount is **not uniform**. It is mildest in the central and near-central
okrugs — Solombalsky at `{python} f"{comp['ratio'].get('Solombalsky', float('nan')):.1f}"`×,
Oktyabrsky at `{python} f"{comp['ratio'].get('Oktyabrsky', float('nan')):.1f}"`×,
Lomonosovsky at `{python} f"{comp['ratio'].get('Lomonosovsky', float('nan')):.1f}"`× —
where specialised alcohol shops are common enough for the export's class to
catch a reasonable share. It is worst in the outlying residential okrugs, where
alcohol is sold almost entirely through grocery chains: Varavino-Faktoriya at
`{python} f"{comp['ratio'].get('Varavino-Faktoriya', float('nan')):.0f}"`× and
Tsiglomensky at `{python} f"{comp['ratio'].get('Tsiglomensky', float('nan')):.0f}"`×.
Any okrug-level risk
comparison built on the export's `Alcohol shops` class alone is therefore biased
**toward the centre** — it understates peripheral exposure more than central
exposure, which is the opposite of the direction a health-equity analysis would
want to be wrong in.

# What this source is good for {#sec-verdict}

- It is the **only source in the project with legal-status semantics**. Every
  other delivery records that an object exists; this one records that it is
  licensed, since when, until when, and whether the licence still stands.
- It carries the **off-trade / on-trade split**, which no commissioned export
  has, and which separates two different exposure mechanisms.
- It is **independent of the contractor** and of 2GIS and OSM alike, so it is a
  genuine external check rather than another view of the same directories.
- It is **free, official and reproducible** — re-downloading the published
  snapshot and re-running one script reproduces the extract exactly.

# Caveats {#sec-caveats}

- **No tobacco.** Despite the regulator's remit, the register contains no
  tobacco licence class. The tobacco risk layer still rests on the commissioned
  exports' 60 objects.
- **Only `{python} f"{n_active / n_rows * 100:.0f}"` % of rows are in force.**
  A count taken without filtering `status` overstates current provision by
  roughly a factor of three, and mixes in addresses vacated years ago.
- **Coordinates cover just over half the extract and are missing
  non-randomly** — older licences lack them, so maps skew recent. Okrug figures
  for `{python} f"{(eg['okrug_source'] == 'street').mean() * 100:.0f}"` % of
  rows rest on a street-name lookup, not a coordinate.
- **Okrug is inferred, never given.** It is borrowed from the third-delivery
  export, so it inherits that export's okrug boundaries and any error in them,
  and the two sources are no longer fully independent at okrug level.
- **The grain is an outlet-licence pair.** `{python} f"{n_rows:,}"` rows are
  `{python} f"{n_lic:,}"` licences at `{python} f"{n_addr:,}"` addresses.
  Counting rows counts neither licences nor outlets.
- **`outlet_region_code` is wrong on 4.2 % of rows** — 88 records carry a
  foreign region code while holding a plain Arkhangelsk address. The extract
  filters on the address for that reason; anyone re-deriving it from the region
  code will lose those records.
- **Novaya Zemlya rows are filed under Arkhangelsk.** Eight records place
  `Белушья Губа` and `Рогачево` — 2,000 km north — inside the city. They carry
  no usable coordinate and are excluded from the maps, but a naive address
  filter keeps them.
- **A licence is not an open shop.** It is a legal permission at an address; it
  does not prove the outlet is trading today, and the register has no closure
  date beyond licence expiry.
